cipher: GIFT-64 round core with the 128-bit key schedule

state_convention.bit_order: state bit i is hexadecimal bit i; bit 0 is the least significant bit
state_convention.nibble_order: S-box j acts on bits 4*j..4*j+3 and bit 4*j is the nibble LSB
state_convention.round_boundary: x[0] is immediately before round-0 AddRoundKey; x[r+1] is immediately after round-r P-layer; x[6] is the compared output boundary

p_layer.semantics: an S-box output bit at source position i is moved to destination P[i]

round_function.constant_rule: for RC[r] bits j=0..5, XOR bit j into state position 4*j+3; XOR constant 1 into state bit 63
round_function.round_key_rule: write W0 bits 0..15, in order, to state positions whose indices modulo 4 are 0 or 1 among positions 0..31; write W1 bits 0..15 analogously to positions 32..63; XOR these 32 bits into the state
round_function.fixed_constants_note: round constants cancel in ordinary XOR-difference propagation but remain part of the concrete two-state executions

key_schedule.initial_words: split the 128-bit master key into W0,...,W7, where Wi contains master-key bits 16*i..16*i+15 and word bit 0 is its LSB
key_schedule.round_key: round r uses the current W0 || W1 under round_key_rule

two_queries.ordinary_difference_model: each SubCells transition need only have nonzero DDT count; round keys are omitted because XOR differences cancel
two_queries.shared_master_key_state_model: there must exist plaintext p and one master key k such that E_k^6(p) xor E_k^6(p xor input_difference) equals output_difference
two_queries.single_key_impossible_definition: the fixed boundary is impossible when the shared-master-key state query is UNSAT

ddt_definition: DDT[a][b] is the number of x in 0..15 such that S(x) xor S(x xor a) = b
